jobs.title: Drift Wood #33 · the map
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 19, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. WOOD usually wears oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn even indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers. CHLOE wears chill tee. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Chloe got in. Wood draws her a map of a city he's never seen. Panel 1: a school newsroom, a thick opened envelope on a desk beside a teenage girl typing who won't look at it, a boy in an overcoat staring at the envelope (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Wood says "It's thick.". Chloe says "Thick is yes.". Panel 2: a teenage boy drawing rapidly on the back of a newspaper proof sheet while a girl watches skeptically (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "I'm making you a map.". Chloe says "You've never been to Seattle.". Wood says "Neither had the people who named the streets.". Panel 3: close-up of a hand-drawn imaginary city map on the back of a proof sheet: hills, water, a needle-shaped tower, an X in the middle and an arrow pointing off the page. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: a teenage girl carefully folding a hand-drawn map into a thick acceptance envelope, a boy beside her, school newsroom (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "It's wrong.". Wood says "I know.". Chloe says "I'm keeping it.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
